evidence: AUTHOR-RECORDED, AND THIS IS AN IRREVERSIBLE-TIER DIFF WHOSE GATE IS NOT SATISFIED — stated first because it is the most important thing in this record. node scripts/classify.mjs returns floor=irreversible, driven by scripts/lib/** BEFORE .github/workflows/ci.yml is even considered. That tier asks for Full review plus 2-of-3 multi-judge plus founder sign-off. This is one author, one model family, no independent reviewer. Do not read this PASS as the tier being met; it is a deterministic-floor record awaiting the panel and the sign-off. WHAT WAS BUILT, AND WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT: a reviewer recommended this narrow check INSTEAD of a recipe runner, after a recipe runner destroyed its own 834-file fixture by extracting a bulk-deletion command from a documentation table and letting bfs — which the harness shadows that command with — execute what the BSD original refuses. This check EXECUTES NOTHING FROM THE CORPUS. It reads text, calls STEPS.length, parseCiSteps() and aliasLinks(), and compares two numbers; scripts/check-figures.test.mjs asserts textually that neither scripts/lib/figures.js nor scripts/check-figures.mjs reaches for child_process, exec*, spawn* at all, so there is no destructive surface to get wrong. It DERIVES rather than greps: parseCiSteps() and /usr/bin/grep -c agree at 44 on the pre-change tree, which is what makes the parser a drop-in rather than a second answer wearing the same name, and a parser cannot be shadowed the way that command was. COVERAGE: 22 figures across docs/STATUS.md and .github/workflows/ci.yml, each an explicit registry entry with a locator and a named derivation. It covers the ten falsified STATUS figures from #102 and the one shadowed grep recipe, because they are the same class. FAILS CLOSED IN THE NAMED DIRECTION: an unmatched locator, a locator matching more than once, a non-finite derivation, a missing file, an unparseable capture and an empty registry are each a FINDING rather than a pass — three of those fired for real on the first run, when three of my own locators were mis-aimed. HISTORICAL FIGURES ARE EXCLUDED DELIBERATELY: markdown blockquote history is stripped, and the control proves the stripping is load-bearing rather than decorative — without it the live floor figure has two candidates in docs/STATUS.md and they are different numbers. NON-VACUITY, BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE CODE SIDE ARRIVED UNPROMPTED: wiring the check added 2 entries to STEPS and 2 steps to ci.yml, moving four derived values, and the new check immediately reported 13 MISMATCHES across both files, each naming file:line, the stated value and the derived one — every one a figure this change had just falsified, reported before it was staged. Document side: one digit edited in docs/STATUS.md gives 'docs/STATUS.md:248 — status-floor-tally states 44, derived 45'. Library side, pure over inputs: a step appended to the workflow TEXT, a STEPS list one shorter, and an alias stripped of links each redden untouched prose. MY FIRST MUTATION TEST WAS SPELLED WITH TODAY'S NUMBER AND WOULD HAVE STOPPED APPLYING: .replace(/now runs \*\*44 steps/) matched nothing once the figure became 46, and a mutation that does not apply is a test that asserts nothing. Its own notEqual guard caught it within the hour; mutations are now driven by the registry entry's own locator. Same shape as the case-spelling control one lane earlier, which is twice in one day that the instrument was wrong before the code was. FIGURES FOUND FALSE OR UNWIREABLE, REPORTED AS FINDINGS: (1) one live figure was UNWIRED and went stale inside this very change — 'would run all 44 checks against an empty workspace' became 46 and nothing said so; now wired. (2) Its neighbour '~45 red steps' was DELETED rather than wired, because a tilde is a promise not to be checked and a figure that cannot be asserted should not be written as a number. (3) A true number inside a false sentence, which this check by construction cannot catch: docs/STATUS.md section 2 says of the six governed && chains that 'its links are steps in their own right, in npm run check and in ci.yml', but check:citations has NEITHER link in STEPS — test:citations is not a step and the other link is a bare node command, and its EXCLUDED reason says so honestly. The three figures around that sentence — 6, 0, 6 — are all correct, which is exactly why a figure check cannot reach it. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, in the code and not only in this record: figures nobody wired (no entry, no check — the checker prints its own coverage so that is a number rather than an impression, and the maintenance cost is one registry line per figure, written down rather than left to be discovered); gh-derived claims, which the sandbox denies by design and which keep the REPORTED marker; historical figures; and whether the sentence around a true number is true.
